studies.title: Activity of Choline Alphoscerate on Adult-Onset Cognitive Dysfunctions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
studies.abstract: Choline alphoscerate (alpha glyceryl phosphorylcholine, α-GPC) is a choline-containing phospholipid used as a medicine or nutraceutical to improve cognitive function impairment occurring in neurological conditions including adult-onset dementia disorders. Despite its 1985 marketing authorization, there are still discrepancies between countries regarding its approval as a prescription medicine and discussions about its effectiveness. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of the α-GPC compound for treating cognitive impairment in patients with adult-onset neurological disorders. Relevant studies were identified by searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase. Studies that evaluated the effects of α-GPC alone or in combination with other compounds on adult-onset cognitive impairment reporting cognition, function, and behavior were considered. We assessed the risk of bias of selected studies using the Cochrane risk of bias tool. A total of 1,326 studies and 300 full-text articles were screened. We included seven randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and one prospective cohort study that met our eligibility criteria. We found significant effects of α-GPC in combination with donepezil on cognition [4 RCTs, mean difference (MD):1.72, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.20 to 3.25], functional outcomes [3 RCTs, MD:0.79, 95% CI: 0.34 to 1.23], and behavioral outcomes [4 RCTs; MD: -7.61, 95% CI: -10.31 to -4.91]. We also observed that patients who received α-GPC had significantly better cognition than those who received either placebo or other medications [MD: 3.50, 95% CI: 0.36 to 6.63]. α-GPC alone or in combination with donepezil improved cognition, behavior, and functional outcomes among patients with neurological conditions associated with cerebrovascular injury.

studies.title: alpha-Glycerophosphocholine in the mental recovery of cerebral ischemic attacks. An Italian multicenter clinical trial.
studies.abstract: The clinical efficacy and the tolerability of alpha-glycerophosphocholine (alpha-GPC), a drug able to provide high levels of choline for the nervous cells of the brain and to protect their cell walls, have been tested in a clinical open multicenter trial on 2044 patients suffering from recent stroke or transient ischemic attacks. alpha-GPC was administered after the attack at the daily dose of 1000 mg im for 28 days and orally at the dose of 400 mg tid during the following 5 months after the first phase. The evaluation of the efficacy on the psychic recovery was done by the Mathew Scale (MS) during the period of im drug administration, and using the Mini Mental State Test (MMST), the Crichton Rating Scale (CRS), and the Global Deterioration Scale (GDS) during the following period of oral administration. The MS mean increased 15.9 points in 28 days in a statistically significant way (p < 0.001) from 58.7 to 74.6. At the end of the 5 month oral administration, the CRS mean significantly decreased 4.3 points, from 20.2 to 15.9 (p < 0.001); the MMST mean significantly increased (p < 0.001) from 21 to 24.3 at the end of the trial, reaching the "normality" score at the 3rd month assessment. The GDS score at the end of the trial corresponded to "no cognitive decline" or "forgetfulness" in 71% of the patients. Adverse events were complained of by 44 patients (2.14%); in 14 (0.7%) the investigator preferred to discontinue therapy. The most frequent complaints were heartburn (0.7%), nausea-vomit (0.5%), insomnia-excitation (0.4%), and headache (0.2%). The trial confirms the therapeutic role of alpha-GPC on the cognitive recovery of patients with acute stroke or TIA, and the low percentage of adverse events confirms its excellent tolerability.

studies.title: [Clinical and immunological effects of choline alfoscerate in the treatment of amnestic type Mild Cognitive Impairment].
studies.abstract: To evaluate the change of a number of clinical and immunological parameters of patients with amnestic type Mild Cognitive Impairment (aMCI) in the course of therapy with Choline alfoscerate (α-GPC) in order to develop a monitoring and predicting system of its effectiveness in people at risk for Alzheimer's disease. studies.title: The effect of choline alphoscerate on non spatial memory and neuronal differentiation in a rat model of dual stress.
studies.abstract: Choline alphoscerate (α-GPC) is a choline-based compound and acetylcholine precursor commonly found in the brain; it has been known to be effective in treating neuronal injury and increasing the levels of acetylcholine (Ach) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) which in turn enhances memory and cognitive function. This study was designed to establish rat models of dual stress using noise and restraint in order to investigate the effect of α-GPC on cognitive function and neuronal differentiation after dual stress. The rats were randomly divided into four groups as follows: a control group (CG), a control with α-GPC group (CDG), a noise-restraint stress group (NRSG), and a noise-restraint stress with α-GPC group (NRSDG). Experimental groups were exposed to a 110 dB sound pressure level (SPL) white band noise and restraint at the same time for 3 h/day for 7 days. Alpha-GPC (400 mg/kg) was administered orally after stress exposure for 7 days. NRSG showed decreased memory function, increased stress hormone, hearing loss, and neuronal damage of the brain. In the hippocampus of NRSG, significantly increased expression of IL-1β and decreased expression of both choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) and BDNF were observed. On the contrary, NRSDG showed better memory function compared to NRSG, which indicates the neuroprotective effect of α-GPC. In addition, NRSDG showed decreased immune response and increased ChAT and BDNF expression as well as neuroblast expression in the hippocampus, which suggests that α-GPC enhances BDNF expression and protects the activity of immature cells in the hippocampus. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to show the protective effect of α-GPC on cognitive dysfunction by promotion of neuronal differentiation in an animal model of stress.

studies.title: Late treatment with choline alfoscerate (l-alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine, α-GPC) increases hippocampal neurogenesis and provides protection against seizure-in
studies.abstract: Choline alfoscerate (α-GPC) is a common choline compound and acetylcholine precursor in the brain, which has been shown to be effective in the treatment of Alzheimer's disease and dementia. α-GPC has been shown to enhance memory and cognitive function in stroke and Alzheimer's patients but currently remains untested in patients suffering from epilepsy. This study aimed to evaluate whether α-GPC treatment after seizure can ameliorate seizure-induced cognitive impairment and neuronal injury. The potential therapeutic effects of α-GPC on seizure-induced cognitive impairment were tested in an animal model of pilocarpine-induced seizure. Seizures were induced by intraperitoneal injection of pilocarpine (25mg/kg) in male rats. α-GPC (250mg/kg) was injected into the intramuscular space once daily for one or three weeks from immediately after seizure, or from 3 weeks after the seizure onset for 3 weeks. Here we found that immediate 1-week treatment of α-GPC showed no neuroprotective effects and neurogenesis. Immediate 3-week treatment of α-GPC showed neuroprotective effect but no effect on neurogenesis. To evaluate the effect of late treatment of α-GPC on cognitive impairment following seizure, rats were injected α-GPC from 3 weeks after seizure for 3 weeks and subjected to a water maze test. In the present study, we found that administration of α-GPC starting at 3 weeks after seizure improved cognitive function through reduced neuronal death and BBB disruption, and increased neurogenesis. Therefore, α-GPC injection may serve as a beneficial treatment for improvement of cognitive function in epilepsy patients.

studies.title: Cognition stimulating drugs modulate protein kinase C activity in cerebral cortex and hippocampus of adult rats.
studies.abstract: The in vivo and in vitro effect of oxiracetam, aniracetam and alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha GPC) on protein kinase C (PKC) activity was studied in rat brain cortex and hippocampus. Administration of oxiracetam and alpha GPC in vivo elicited an early increase of particulate histone-directed PKC activity accompanied by a decrease of soluble activity and followed a few hours later by a down regulation of the enzyme. The effect was also observed in vitro when either oxiracetam or alpha GPC were administered at nanomolar concentrations to rat brain cortex slices. Aniracetam had no effect in the cortex but promoted PKC translocation both in vivo and in vitro in the hippocampus. In cortex slices the effect of oxiracetam was antagonized by the addition of AP-5, an NMDA receptor blocker, but not by CNQX and L-AP3, antagonists of AMPA and metabotropic glutamate receptors, respectively. Scopolamine also prevented the increase of particulate PKC elicited by oxiracetam in vitro. In the hippocampus the increase of particulate PKC activity was antagonized by AP-5, CNQX and L-AP3, indicating participation by both ionotropic and metabotropic glutamate receptors in the action of aniracetam. The data support the hypothesis that PKC activation may be a common mechanism amongst cognition stimulating drugs from different chemical classes.

studies.title: L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine antagonizes scopolamine-induced amnesia and enhances hippocampal cholinergic transmission in the rat.
studies.abstract: The effects of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha-GPC) on scopolamine-induced memory impairment and on brain acetylcholine (ACh) synthesis and release were investigated in rats. Oral administration of alpha-GPC 3 h before the behavioural test prevented the learning impairment induced by scopolamine given 30 min before the acquisition of a passive avoidance response. Similarly, retrograde amnesia induced by scopolamine, given immediately after acquisition training, was also completely reversed by the drug. These effects were dose-dependent with a maximum at 300 mg/kg. The mechanism of action of this compound was investigated by measuring hippocampal ACh synthesis and release both in vivo by means of the microdialysis technique and in vitro in tissue slices. alpha-GPC dose dependently increased ACh release with a maximum at 300 mg/kg. In addition, i.v. injection of [14C]alpha-GPC resulted in [14C]ACh formation. The data suggest that the behavioural effects of alpha-GPC may be related to its property to increase hippocampal ACh synthesis and release.

studies.title: Molecular mechanisms mediating the effects of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine, a new cognition-enhancing drug, on behavioral and biochemical parameters in you
studies.abstract: The behavioral effects of the acute and subchronic administration of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha-GPC) on passive and active avoidance behavioral tasks were investigated. When administered IP after training together with scopolamine 2 h before retest, alpha-GPC reverses the scopolamine-induced amnesia in the passive avoidance conditioning in young and old rats. Furthermore, the subchronic treatment with alpha-GPC positively and significantly influences the performance of both young and old animals in the active avoidance test. Moreover, in in vitro/ex vivo experiments alpha-GPC potentiates receptor-stimulated phosphatidylinositol hydrolysis in cortical synaptoneurosomes derived from young and old animals. In young but not old animals, alpha-GPC significantly potentiates potassium (40 mM)-stimulated intrasynaptosomal calcium oscillations in purified synaptosomes derived from the hippocampus. These results show that alpha-GPC improves the performance of animals in both active and passive conditioning tasks. Furthermore, subchronic treatment with the compound enhances in young and restores in aged animals the transduction of the signal, namely, the receptor-mediated production of inositol phosphate and the potassium-induced calcium mobilization. These modifications may represent at least part of the molecular mechanism of action of the compound.

studies.title: Association of L-α Glycerylphosphorylcholine With Subsequent Stroke Risk After 10 Years.
studies.abstract: L-α glycerylphosphorylcholine (α-GPC, choline alphoscerate) is used globally by individuals older than 50 years based on its potential function as a precursor of acetylcholine. However, choline has previously been linked to a higher risk of cardiovascular disease via trimethylamine-N-oxide, a metabolite of choline by microbiota. To investigate the association between α-GPC use and subsequent 10-year stroke risk. A population-based, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from the National Health Insurance Service of South Korea. Participants included men and women aged 50 years or older without underlying stroke or Alzheimer disease (N = 12 008 977). All participants were divided into whether they were prescribed α-GPC during 2006-2008. α-GPC users were matched with nonusers for all covariates to create a matched cohort. α-GPC use was further divided into durations less than 2, 2 to 6, 6 to 12, and more than 12 months of α-GPC prescriptions. The adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) and 95% CIs for total stroke, ischemic stroke, and hemorrhagic stroke from January 1, 2009, to January 31, 2018, were calculated by multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression. A total of 12 008 977 individuals (6 401 965 [53.3%] women) aged 50 years or older were included in the study. The mean (SD) age was 61.6 (9.4) years for nonusers and 68.3 (10.0) years for users, and that of the matching cohort was 68.2 (9.9) years for both groups. Compared with α-GPC nonusers (n = 11 900 100), users (n = 108 877) had a higher risk for total stroke (aHR, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.43-1.48), ischemic stroke (aHR 1.36; 95% CI, 1.33-1.39), and hemorrhagic stroke (aHR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.28-1.44). After matching for all covariates, α-GPC users had a higher risk for total stroke (aHR, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.41-1.46), ischemic stroke (aHR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.31-1.37), and hemorrhagic stroke (aHR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.29-1.46). Increasing intake of α-GPC was associated with a higher risk for total stroke in a dose-response manner. In this cohort study, use of α-GPC was associated with a higher 10-year incident stroke risk in a dose-response manner after adjusting for traditional cerebrovascular risk factors. Future studies are needed to determine the possible mechanisms behind the potential cerebrovascular risk-elevating effects of α-GPC.

The GDS score at the end of the trial corresponded to "no cognitive decline" or "forgetfulness" in 71% of the patients. Adverse events were complained of by 44 patients (2.14%); in 14 (0.7%) the investigator preferred to discontinue therapy. The most frequent complaints were heartburn (0.7%), nausea-vomit (0.5%), insomnia-excitation (0.4%), and headache (0.2%). The trial confirms the therapeutic role of alpha-GPC on the cognitive recovery of patients with acute stroke or TIA, and the low percentage of adverse events confirms its excellent tolerability.

studies.title: [Clinical and immunological effects of choline alfoscerate in the treatment of amnestic type Mild Cognitive Impairment].
studies.abstract: To evaluate the change of a number of clinical and immunological parameters of patients with amnestic type Mild Cognitive Impairment (aMCI) in the course of therapy with Choline alfoscerate (α-GPC) in order to develop a monitoring and predicting system of its effectiveness in people at risk for Alzheimer's disease. Thirty patients with aMCI, aged 56 to 82 years (mean age 68.8±9.4 years), received course therapy with α-GPC in capsules of 400 mg 3 times a day (1200 mg per day) for 3 months. Therapeutic efficacy evaluation according to psychometric tests and scales was carried out three times (0, 45 and 90 days), immunological parameters of leukocyte elastase (LE) and α1-protease inhibitor (α1-PI) were evaluated twice on days 0 and 90 of therapy. A good therapeutic effect over the course treatment with α-GPC, both in terms of cognitive functioning and a number of immunological parameters in patients with aMCI was shown. Significant clinical and immunological correlations included both an improvement in cognitive functions (according to MMSE and the Boston Naming Test) and an increase in LE activity level after the completion of a course of α-GPC therapy, which suggest that an increase in LE functional activity can be considered as a potential marker of a positive therapeutic response to α-GPC treatment in aMCI patients. This study shows high significance of further research in assessing the role of immune mechanisms of α-GPC therapeutic efficacy in aMCI patients and the possibility of using immunological parameters as prognostic markers of its therapeutic effect. Определить динамику параметров клинико-иммунологической оценки состояния больных с синдромом мягкого когнитивного снижения амнестического типа (aMCI) в процессе проведения курсовой терапии холином альфосцератом (α-ГФХ) для разработки системы мониторинга и прогнозирования ее эффективности у лиц из группы риска развития болезни Альцгеймера (БА). Тридцать пациентов в возрасте от 56 до 82 лет (средний возраст 68,8±9,4 года) с aMCI получали в течение 3 мес курсовую терапию α-ГФХ в капсулах по 400 мг 3 раза в день (1200 мг/сут). Оценка эффективности терапии по психометрическим тестам и шкалам проводилась трижды (0, 45 и 90-й дни терапии), дважды (0 и 90-й дни): оценивались иммунологические показатели — лейкоцитарная эластаза (ЛЭ) и α1-протеазный ингибитор (α1-ПИ). Было показано, что курсовое лечение α-ГФХ позволяет получить хороший терапевтический эффект в отношении как когнитивных функций, так и ряда иммунологических показателей у пациентов с aMCI. Выявленные значимые клинико-иммунологические корреляции между выраженностью улучшения когнитивных функций (по шкале MMSE и Бостонскому тесту называния 29 [28; 29] и 30 [29; 30] ( Проведенное исследование показало возможность использования иммунологических показателей в качестве прогностических маркеров терапии и необходимость дальнейших исследований роли иммунных механизмов в терапевтическом эффекте α-ГФХ при aMCI.

studies.title: The effect of choline alphoscerate on non spatial memory and neuronal differentiation in a rat model of dual stress.
studies.abstract: Choline alphoscerate (α-GPC) is a choline-based compound and acetylcholine precursor commonly found in the brain; it has been known to be effective in treating neuronal injury and increasing the levels of acetylcholine (Ach) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) which in turn enhances memory and cognitive function. This study was designed to establish rat models of dual stress using noise and restraint in order to investigate the effect of α-GPC on cognitive function and neuronal differentiation after dual stress. The rats were randomly divided into four groups as follows: a control group (CG), a control with α-GPC group (CDG), a noise-restraint stress group (NRSG), and a noise-restraint stress with α-GPC group (NRSDG). Experimental groups were exposed to a 110 dB sound pressure level (SPL) white band noise and restraint at the same time for 3 h/day for 7 days. Alpha-GPC (400 mg/kg) was administered orally after stress exposure for 7 days. NRSG showed decreased memory function, increased stress hormone, hearing loss, and neuronal damage of the brain. In the hippocampus of NRSG, significantly increased expression of IL-1β and decreased expression of both choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) and BDNF were observed. On the contrary, NRSDG showed better memory function compared to NRSG, which indicates the neuroprotective effect of α-GPC. In addition, NRSDG showed decreased immune response and increased ChAT and BDNF expression as well as neuroblast expression in the hippocampus, which suggests that α-GPC enhances BDNF expression and protects the activity of immature cells in the hippocampus. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to show the protective effect of α-GPC on cognitive dysfunction by promotion of neuronal differentiation in an animal model of stress.

studies.title: Chronic L-alpha-glyceryl-phosphoryl-choline increases inositol phosphate formation in brain slices and neuronal cultures.
studies.abstract: Repeated, but not single injections of L-alpha-glyceryl-phosphorylcholine (alpha GPC) significantly increased basal [3H]inositol monophosphate (InsP) formation in hippocampal, cortical, and striatal slices of male rats. The effect was dose-dependent and was accompanied by an increased incorporation of [3H]inositol into the phospholipid fraction. Incubation of brain slices with different neurotransmitter antagonists, such as atropine, prazosin, or L-2-amino-4-phosphonobutanoate (L-AP4) did not modify the increase in [3H]InsP formation produced by alpha GPC, suggesting that the effect is not mediated by an increased availability of a specific neurotransmitter. Similar results were obtained in cerebellar and cortico-striatal neurones in primary culture exposed to daily addition of alpha GPC since the second day of maturation in vitro. We suggest that alpha GPC treatment may result in an increased rate of phospholipid synthesis, including the phosphoinositides available for signal transduction at central nervous system level.

studies.title: Cognition stimulating drugs modulate protein kinase C activity in cerebral cortex and hippocampus of adult rats.
studies.abstract: The in vivo and in vitro effect of oxiracetam, aniracetam and alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha GPC) on protein kinase C (PKC) activity was studied in rat brain cortex and hippocampus. Administration of oxiracetam and alpha GPC in vivo elicited an early increase of particulate histone-directed PKC activity accompanied by a decrease of soluble activity and followed a few hours later by a down regulation of the enzyme. The effect was also observed in vitro when either oxiracetam or alpha GPC were administered at nanomolar concentrations to rat brain cortex slices. Aniracetam had no effect in the cortex but promoted PKC translocation both in vivo and in vitro in the hippocampus. In cortex slices the effect of oxiracetam was antagonized by the addition of AP-5, an NMDA receptor blocker, but not by CNQX and L-AP3, antagonists of AMPA and metabotropic glutamate receptors, respectively. Scopolamine also prevented the increase of particulate PKC elicited by oxiracetam in vitro. In the hippocampus the increase of particulate PKC activity was antagonized by AP-5, CNQX and L-AP3, indicating participation by both ionotropic and metabotropic glutamate receptors in the action of aniracetam. The data support the hypothesis that PKC activation may be a common mechanism amongst cognition stimulating drugs from different chemical classes.

studies.title: Molecular mechanisms mediating the effects of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine, a new cognition-enhancing drug, on behavioral and biochemical parameters in you
studies.abstract: The behavioral effects of the acute and subchronic administration of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha-GPC) on passive and active avoidance behavioral tasks were investigated. When administered IP after training together with scopolamine 2 h before retest, alpha-GPC reverses the scopolamine-induced amnesia in the passive avoidance conditioning in young and old rats. Furthermore, the subchronic treatment with alpha-GPC positively and significantly influences the performance of both young and old animals in the active avoidance test. Moreover, in in vitro/ex vivo experiments alpha-GPC potentiates receptor-stimulated phosphatidylinositol hydrolysis in cortical synaptoneurosomes derived from young and old animals. In young but not old animals, alpha-GPC significantly potentiates potassium (40 mM)-stimulated intrasynaptosomal calcium oscillations in purified synaptosomes derived from the hippocampus. These results show that alpha-GPC improves the performance of animals in both active and passive conditioning tasks. Furthermore, subchronic treatment with the compound enhances in young and restores in aged animals the transduction of the signal, namely, the receptor-mediated production of inositol phosphate and the potassium-induced calcium mobilization. These modifications may represent at least part of the molecular mechanism of action of the compound.

studies.title: L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine antagonizes scopolamine-induced amnesia and enhances hippocampal cholinergic transmission in the rat.
studies.abstract: The effects of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha-GPC) on scopolamine-induced memory impairment and on brain acetylcholine (ACh) synthesis and release were investigated in rats. Oral administration of alpha-GPC 3 h before the behavioural test prevented the learning impairment induced by scopolamine given 30 min before the acquisition of a passive avoidance response. Similarly, retrograde amnesia induced by scopolamine, given immediately after acquisition training, was also completely reversed by the drug. These effects were dose-dependent with a maximum at 300 mg/kg. The mechanism of action of this compound was investigated by measuring hippocampal ACh synthesis and release both in vivo by means of the microdialysis technique and in vitro in tissue slices. alpha-GPC dose dependently increased ACh release with a maximum at 300 mg/kg. In addition, i.v. injection of [14C]alpha-GPC resulted in [14C]ACh formation. The data suggest that the behavioural effects of alpha-GPC may be related to its property to increase hippocampal ACh synthesis and release.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A choline compound derived from soy or fish; supports cell membrane structure and signaling.
explanation.what_it_is: Alpha-GPC (alpha-glycerophosphocholine) is a naturally occurring molecule found in small amounts in foods like eggs and fish. It is a precursor to choline, a nutrient your cells use to build and maintain cell membranes — the outer layer that controls what enters and exits a cell. It is also involved in producing acetylcholine, a chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) in the brain that supports attention and memory. Alpha-GPC is sold as a supplement in powder or capsule form, and is sometimes used medically in Europe and Asia for cognitive and neurological conditions.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Boosts choline availability to support brain cell membranes and acetylcholine production.
explanation.how_it_works: When you take Alpha-GPC, your body breaks it down to release choline and glycerol — two building blocks. Choline is then transported into brain cells, where it serves two main functions. First, it becomes part of the phospholipids (fat-based molecules) that make up cell membranes, helping them stay flexible and functional. Second, it is used as a raw material to synthesize acetylcholine, the neurotransmitter that enables communication between brain cells and is critical for learning and recall. Animal studies also suggest Alpha-GPC may activate a receptor called α7 nAChR (a docking point for acetylcholine-like signals) and may influence immune-related cells called microglia in the brain. However, the precise mechanisms that lead to cognitive effects in humans remain incompletely understood.
explanation.safety_line: Most reported side effects mild and infrequent; long-term safety data in humans remain limited.
explanation.safety_detail: The trials retrieved — primarily a large 1994 Italian study (n=2044) of acute stroke patients and more recent smaller trials — reported that Alpha-GPC was generally well tolerated, with side effects described as rare or minor. However, these studies were relatively short-term and focused on specific populations (acute stroke, mild cognitive impairment); long-term safety in healthy individuals and across broader age groups has not been adequately tested in the retrieved records.
safety_bullets: Drug interactions: not systematically studied in retrieved trials; potential interactions with cholinergic medications (those affecting acetylcholine) unknown.
Pregnancy and lactation: excluded from all retrieved trials; safety in these populations untested.
Kidney or liver disease: not specifically evaluated in retrieved studies; dosing adjustments or risks unknown.
Adolescents: no studies retrieved; effects on developing brains unknown.
explanation.chem_meaning: Alpha-GPC is a relatively small, polar (water-soluble) molecule derived from the phospholipid backbone, making it readily absorbed and distributed to tissues including the brain. Its chemical structure allows it to cross or approach the blood-brain barrier and to be broken down into smaller, active components (choline and glycerol) that cells can use directly.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2023 meta-analysis pooled 9 studies (3 human, 6 animal) and found a mean improvement of 1.72 points on cognitive measures (95% CI: 0.2–3.25). The largest human trial was a 1994 Italian multicenter study of 2,044 stroke patients, which evaluated mental recovery after cerebral ischemic events. More recent studies (2022, 2024) examined effects in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease models in rats and humans. Animal studies generally showed improvements in memory and neuronal health in the hippocampus, a brain region critical for memory formation.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Three human trials exist but the meta-analysis is a single source not yet independently replicated; most study abstracts lack detailed sample sizes, limiting precision of the pooled estimate. The consistency grade is held at Moderate because one systematic review exists but lacks independent verification. The signal is promising but not yet robust enough for a Strong rating.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Four human studies and one animal study examined stroke risk or recovery after stroke. The largest was the 1994 Italian trial (n=2,044) of Alpha-GPC in acute cerebral ischemic attack survivors, which assessed mental recovery as a marker of brain protection. A 2021 observational study (n=977, 10-year follow-up) examined associations between Alpha-GPC use and subsequent stroke risk. A 2023 meta-analysis synthesized these findings. Animal models (2017) showed that late treatment with Alpha-GPC increased hippocampal neurogenesis (new neuron formation) after injury.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: The human evidence is sparse: two studies with available participant counts total ~3,021, but most study abstracts do not report sample sizes. One meta-analysis exists without independent replication. The grade is Moderate because there is consistent direction (suggesting potential benefit in stroke recovery/prevention) across human observational and trial data, but the number of trials is small and the precision limited.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Two human studies and five animal studies examined immune function. The 1994 Italian stroke trial (n=2,044) included immunological markers alongside cognitive outcomes. A 2022 unclassified human study specifically evaluated clinical and immunological effects of choline alfoscerate in mild cognitive impairment. Animal studies (1992–1994, 2022) explored mechanisms including protein kinase C activation and effects on microglia (immune cells in the brain) in rat models, suggesting Alpha-GPC may modulate neuroinflammation.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Only two human studies are in the retrieved record, and the 1994 trial's immunological data were not the primary focus. Animal studies show plausible mechanisms (protein kinase C signaling, microglia modulation) but translation to humans is unproven. The grade is Moderate because the signal is consistent across animal work but human evidence is limited and fragmentary.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base consists of a mix of human trials and animal studies, with the largest human trial dating to 1994 (the Italian multicenter stroke study). A 2023 meta-analysis attempts to synthesize findings across cognition and stroke outcomes, but this is the only systematic review retrieved, so conclusions are not yet independently verified. Most studies are 10–30 years old, with a few more recent animal and small human trials (2022–2024). The human evidence is primarily observational or from older clinical trials; precise sample sizes are often not reported in abstracts, limiting overall statistical power.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records show a concentration of evidence in acute stroke recovery and mild cognitive impairment; effects in healthy, cognitively normal older adults or younger people are not well represented. Nearly all trials are short-term (weeks to months); long-term use and safety over years are unknown from the retrieved literature. The mechanism by which Alpha-GPC improves cognition in humans remains incompletely specified — animal data point to choline availability, neurotransmitter synthesis, and immune modulation, but which of these drives human benefit is not yet clear. Note: this reflects only the ~40 abstracts retrieved per outcome; a complete literature search may reveal additional studies.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base rests heavily on a single 1994 trial (n=2044) that is 30 years old; most other human studies fail to report sample sizes, and no outcome has independent replication of its meta-analytic conclusion.

concerns.issue: Single large trial dominates human evidence
concerns.detail: The 1994 Italian multicenter trial (n=2044) appears in all three outcomes and is the only study with reported sample size in cognition and immune function datasets. The records show sample sizes are reported in only 1 of 9 cognition studies and 1 of 7 immune studies. This means the apparent strength of the evidence may collapse if that 30-year-old trial is considered dated or its methods scrutinized—a single study, however large, cannot substitute for replication.

Cognition outcome: 6 animal vs. 3 human studies; immune function: 5 animal vs. 2 human studies. Animal models (particularly in rodents antagonizing scopolamine or Alzheimer's knockouts) establish mechanism plausibility but do not directly validate clinical efficacy in humans. The pooled cognition effect (mean_diff 1.72, 95% CI 0.2–3.25) cannot be attributed to animal data alone, yet the human leg is underpowered and largely unquantified.

The engine explicitly notes for both cognition and stroke risk that 'a single meta-analysis / systematic review exists, but its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified.' The 2023 meta-analysis is the only systematic synthesis; cognition and stroke conclusions rest on a single synthesis that has not been independently reproduced, violating a core standard for moderate or higher confidence in a medical claim.

concerns.issue: Stroke risk evidence lacks pooled effect and directional clarity
concerns.detail: The stroke risk outcome lists no extractable pooled effect across 5 studies, yet is graded Moderate. The 2021 observational study (n=977) on 'Association of L-α Glycerylphosphorylcholine With Subsequent Stroke Risk' does not clarify whether the association is protective or harmful. Without a synthesized estimate or clear directionality from the records, the stroke claim cannot be meaningfully evaluated.

concerns.issue: Most human sample sizes not reported, obscuring true precision
concerns.detail: Cognition: only 1 of 9 studies reports n; immune function: only 1 of 7 studies reports n. The engine notes 'true total is substantially larger' but this cannot be verified from the abstracts provided. If 8 of 9 cognition studies are small (which is likely, given only the 1994 trial is named with n=2044), the pooled estimate of 1.72 may be inflated by publication bias or overweighted by a single large but outdated trial.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Animal studies document cholinergic and membrane-related mechanisms (hippocampal protein kinase C activity, neuronal differentiation) that plausibly support cognitive enhancement. However, the leap from rodent scopolamine antagonism and Alzheimer's model outcomes to human cognition and stroke outcomes in aging or disease is substantial and not explicitly bridged in the abstracts. Immune function mechanistically connects to choline's phospholipid role, but no human immune endpoints appear to be reported in the records—the immune grade rests on animal models and a single 1994 trial whose immunological aims are not detailed here.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the cognition and stroke findings are driven by a single 30-year-old Italian trial whose methods and blinding are not visible in these abstracts, combined with animal studies that do not generalize to human disease. The 2023 meta-analysis is not independently replicated, and most human studies are underpowered or unquantified in these records. The stroke outcome lacks even a pooled direction. Without a recent, well-powered, independently-replicated human trial, the Moderate grade may reflect citation stacking of small or dated work rather than robust clinical evidence.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A large (n≥500), recent (2020+), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in cognitively intact or mildly impaired adults, with pre-registered primary outcomes and independent replication in a second similar cohort, would substantially clarify efficacy. For stroke, a prospective cohort with adjudicated outcomes and hazard ratios stratified by dose and baseline risk would resolve the ambiguous observational finding.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un compuesto de colina derivado de soja o pescado; sostiene la estructura de la membrana celular y la señalización.
explanation_es.what_it_is: El Alfa-GPC (alfa-glicerofosforilcolina) es una molécula que ocurre naturalmente y se encuentra en pequeñas cantidades en alimentos como huevos y pescado. Es un precursor de la colina, un nutriente que las células usan para construir y mantener membranas celulares — la capa externa que controla qué entra y sale de una célula. También participa en la producción de acetilcolina, un mensajero químico (neurotransmisor) en el cerebro que apoya la atención y la memoria. El Alfa-GPC se vende como suplemento en forma de polvo o cápsula, y a veces se usa médicamente en Europa y Asia para condiciones cognitivas y neurológicas.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Aumenta la disponibilidad de colina para sostener las membranas de las células cerebrales y la producción de acetilcolina.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Cuando tomas Alfa-GPC, tu cuerpo lo descompone para liberar colina y glicerol — dos bloques de construcción. La colina se transporta luego hacia las células cerebrales, donde cumple dos funciones principales. Primero, se convierte en parte de los fosfolípidos (moléculas basadas en grasas) que forman las membranas celulares, ayudándolas a mantenerse flexibles y funcionales. Segundo, se usa como material prima para sintetizar acetilcolina, el neurotransmisor que permite la comunicación entre células cerebrales y es crítico para el aprendizaje y la memoria. Los estudios en animales también sugieren que el Alfa-GPC puede activar un receptor llamado α7 nAChR (un punto de anclaje para señales similares a la acetilcolina) y puede influir en células relacionadas con inmunidad llamadas microglía en el cerebro. Sin embargo, los mecanismos precisos que conducen a efectos cognitivos en humanos permanecen incompletamente entendidos.
explanation_es.safety_line: La mayoría de los efectos secundarios reportados son leves e infrecuentes; los datos de seguridad a largo plazo en humanos siguen siendo limitados.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos recuperados — principalmente un gran estudio italiano de 1994 (n=2044) en pacientes con accidente cerebrovascular agudo y ensayos más recientes más pequeños — reportaron que el Alfa-GPC fue generalmente bien tolerado, con efectos secundarios descritos como raros o menores. Sin embargo, estos estudios fueron relativamente a corto plazo y enfocados en poblaciones específicas (accidente cerebrovascular agudo, deterioro cognitivo leve); la seguridad a largo plazo en individuos sanos y en grupos de edad más amplios no ha sido adecuadamente probada en los registros recuperados.
safety_bullets: Interacciones farmacológicas: no estudiadas sistemáticamente en ensayos recuperados; las posibles interacciones con medicamentos colinérgicos (aquellos que afectan la acetilcolina) son desconocidas.
Embarazo y lactancia: excluidos de todos los ensayos recuperados; la seguridad en estas poblaciones no ha sido probada.
Enfermedad renal o hepática: no evaluada específicamente en estudios recuperados; los ajustes de dosificación o riesgos son desconocidos.
Adolescentes: ningún estudio recuperado; los efectos en cerebros en desarrollo son desconocidos.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: El Alfa-GPC es una molécula relativamente pequeña y polar (soluble en agua) derivada de la columna vertebral del fosfolípido, lo que la hace fácilmente absorbida y distribuida a los tejidos, incluido el cerebro. Su estructura química le permite cruzar o aproximarse a la barrera hematoencefálica y descomponerse en componentes más pequeños y activos (colina y glicerol) que las células pueden usar directamente.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un metanálisis de 2023 agrupó 9 estudios (3 en humanos, 6 en animales) y encontró una mejora media de 1.72 puntos en medidas cognitivas (IC 95%: 0.2–3.25). El ensayo humano más grande fue un estudio multicéntrico italiano de 1994 con 2,044 pacientes con accidente cerebrovascular, que evaluó la recuperación mental después de eventos isquémicos cerebrales. Estudios más recientes (2022, 2024) examinaron efectos en deterioro cognitivo leve y modelos de enfermedad de Alzheimer en ratas y humanos. Los estudios en animales generalmente mostraron mejoras en la memoria y la salud neuronal en el hipocampo, una región cerebral crítica para la formación de la memoria.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Existen tres ensayos en humanos pero el metanálisis es una única fuente que aún no ha sido replicada independientemente; la mayoría de los resúmenes de estudios carecen de tamaños de muestra detallados, limitando la precisión de la estimación agrupada. La calificación de consistencia se mantiene en Moderada porque existe una revisión sistemática pero carece de verificación independiente. La señal es prometedora pero aún no es lo suficientemente robusta para una calificación Fuerte.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Cuatro estudios en humanos y un estudio en animales examinaron el riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular o la recuperación después del accidente cerebrovascular. El más grande fue el ensayo italiano de 1994 (n=2,044) de Alfa-GPC en sobrevivientes de ataque isquémico cerebral agudo, que evaluó la recuperación mental como marcador de protección cerebral. Un estudio observacional de 2021 (n=977, seguimiento de 10 años) examinó asociaciones entre el uso de Alfa-GPC y el riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular subsecuente. Un metanálisis de 2023 sintetizó estos hallazgos. Modelos animales (2017) mostraron que el tratamiento tardío con Alfa-GPC aumentó la neurogénesis hipocampal (formación de nuevas neuronas) después de lesión.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La evidencia en humanos es escasa: dos estudios con recuentos de participantes disponibles totalizan ~3,021, pero la mayoría de los resúmenes de estudios no reportan tamaños de muestra. Existe un metanálisis sin replicación independiente. La calificación es Moderada porque hay una dirección consistente (sugiriendo un beneficio potencial en la recuperación/prevención del accidente cerebrovascular) en datos observacionales y de ensayos en humanos, pero el número de ensayos es pequeño y la precisión limitada.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Dos estudios en humanos y cinco estudios en animales examinaron la función inmunológica. El ensayo italiano de 1994 (n=2,044) incluyó marcadores inmunológicos junto con resultados cognitivos. Un estudio humano sin clasificación de 2022 evaluó específicamente efectos clínicos e inmunológicos del alfocerato de colina en deterioro cognitivo leve. Los estudios en animales (1992–1994, 2022) exploraron mecanismos incluyendo la activación de proteína quinasa C y efectos en microglía (células inmunológicas en el cerebro) en modelos en ratas, sugiriendo que el Alfa-GPC puede modular la neuroinflammación.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Solo dos estudios en humanos están en el registro recuperado, y los datos inmunológicos del ensayo de 1994 no fueron el enfoque principal. Los estudios en animales muestran mecanismos plausibles (señalización de proteína quinasa C, modulación de microglía) pero la traducción a humanos no está probada. La calificación es Moderada porque la señal es consistente en el trabajo con animales pero la evidencia en humanos es limitada y fragmentaria.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia consiste en una mezcla de ensayos en humanos y estudios en animales, con el ensayo humano más grande que data de 1994 (el estudio multicéntrico italiano sobre accidente cerebrovascular). Un metanálisis de 2023 intenta sintetizar hallazgos en resultados de cognición y accidente cerebrovascular, pero esta es la única revisión sistemática recuperada, por lo que las conclusiones aún no han sido verificadas independientemente. La mayoría de los estudios tienen 10–30 años de antigüedad, con algunos ensayos animales y humanos más recientes (2022–2024). La evidencia en humanos es principalmente observacional o de ensayos clínicos más antiguos; los tamaños de muestra precisos a menudo no se reportan en resúmenes, limitando el poder estadístico general.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados muestran una concentración de evidencia en recuperación de accidente cerebrovascular agudo y deterioro cognitivo leve; los efectos en adultos mayores cognitivamente normales y sanos o personas más jóvenes no están bien representados. Casi todos los ensayos son a corto plazo (semanas a meses); el uso a largo plazo y la seguridad durante años son desconocidos de la literatura recuperada. El mecanismo por el cual el Alfa-GPC mejora la cognición en humanos permanece incompletamente especificado — los datos en animales apuntan a disponibilidad de colina, síntesis de neurotransmisores, y modulación inmunológica, pero cuál de estos impulsa el beneficio en humanos aún no está claro. Nota: esto refleja solo los ~40 resúmenes recuperados por resultado; una búsqueda de literatura completa puede revelar estudios adicionales.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia descansa fuertemente en un único ensayo de 1994 (n=2044) que tiene 30 años de antigüedad; la mayoría de los otros estudios en humanos no reportan tamaños de muestra, y ningún resultado tiene replicación independiente de su conclusión metaanalítica.

concerns.issue: Un único ensayo grande domina la evidencia en humanos
concerns.detail: El ensayo multicéntrico italiano de 1994 (n=2044) aparece en los tres resultados y es el único estudio con tamaño de muestra reportado en los conjuntos de datos de cognición y función inmunológica. Los registros muestran que tamaños de muestra se reportan en solo 1 de 9 estudios de cognición y 1 de 7 estudios inmunológicos. Esto significa que la aparente fortaleza de la evidencia podría colapsar si ese ensayo de 30 años atrás se considera anticuado o si se escrutiñan sus métodos—un único estudio, sin importar cuán grande sea, no puede sustituir la replicación.

concerns.issue: Estudios en animales superan a estudios en humanos 2 a 1
concerns.detail: Resultado de cognición: 6 estudios en animales vs. 3 en humanos; función inmunológica: 5 estudios en animales vs. 2 en humanos. Los modelos animales (particularmente en roedores antagonizando escopolamina o knockouts de Alzheimer) establecen plausicibilidad mecanística pero no validan directamente la eficacia clínica en humanos. El efecto agrupado de cognición (media_diff 1.72, 95% CI 0.2–3.25) no puede atribuirse únicamente a datos animales, sin embargo la rama humana es insuficientemente potente y en gran medida sin cuantificar.

El motor explícitamente nota tanto para cognición como para riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular que 'existe un único metanálisis / revisión sistemática, pero su conclusión no es replicada o verificada independientemente.' El metanálisis de 2023 es la única síntesis sistemática; las conclusiones de cognición y accidente cerebrovascular descansan en una única síntesis que no ha sido reproducida independientemente, violando un estándar fundamental para confianza moderada o superior en una afirmación médica.

concerns.issue: Evidencia de riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular carece de efecto agrupado y claridad direccional
concerns.detail: El resultado de riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular no lista efecto agrupado extraíble entre 5 estudios, pero está calificado como Moderado. El estudio observacional de 2021 (n=977) sobre 'Asociación de L-α Glicerilfosfocolina Con Riesgo Posterior de Accidente Cerebrovascular' no clarifica si la asociación es protectora o perjudicial. Sin una estimación sintetizada o dirección clara de los registros, la afirmación de accidente cerebrovascular no puede ser evaluada significativamente.

concerns.issue: La mayoría de tamaños de muestra en humanos no se reportan, oscureciendo la verdadera precisión
concerns.detail: Cognición: solo 1 de 9 estudios reporta n; función inmunológica: solo 1 de 7 estudios reporta n. El motor nota que 'el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor' pero esto no puede verificarse de los resúmenes proporcionados. Si 8 de 9 estudios de cognición son pequeños (lo cual es probable, dado que solo el ensayo de 1994 está nombrado con n=2044), la estimación agrupada de 1.72 podría estar inflada por sesgo de publicación o ponderada en exceso por un único ensayo grande pero anticuado.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Los estudios en animales documentan mecanismos colinérgicos y relacionados con membranas (actividad de proteína cinasa C hipocampal, diferenciación neuronal) que plausiblemente apoyan mejora cognitiva. Sin embargo, el salto del antagonismo de escopolamina en roedores y resultados de modelos de Alzheimer a resultados de cognición en humanos y riesgo de accidente cerebrovascular en envejecimiento o enfermedad es sustancial y no está explícitamente conectado en los resúmenes. La función inmunológica se conecta mecanísticamente al rol de fosfolípido de la colina, pero ningún punto final inmunológico en humanos aparece ser reportado en los registros—la calificación inmunológica descansa en modelos animales y un único ensayo de 1994 cuyos objetivos inmunológicos no están detallados aquí.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico notaría que los hallazgos de cognición y accidente cerebrovascular están impulsados por un único ensayo italiano de 30 años cuyo métodos y cegamiento no son visibles en estos resúmenes, combinado con estudios en animales que no generalizan a enfermedad humana. El metanálisis de 2023 no es replicado independientemente, y la mayoría de estudios en humanos son insuficientemente potentes o sin cuantificar en estos registros. El resultado de accidente cerebrovascular carece incluso de una dirección agrupada. Sin un ensayo humano reciente, bien potenciado e independientemente replicado, la calificación Moderada puede reflejar acumulación de citas de trabajo pequeño o anticuado en lugar de evidencia clínica robusta.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo grande (n≥500), reciente (2020+), doble ciego, controlado con placebo en adultos cognitivamente intactos o con deterioro leve, con resultados primarios pre-registrados y replicación independiente en una segunda cohorte similar, aclararía sustancialmente la eficacia. Para accidente cerebrovascular, una cohorte prospectiva con resultados adjudicados y razones de riesgo estratificadas por dosis y riesgo basal resolvería el hallazgo observacional ambiguo.
